answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 18 July 1950 · founder of the Virgin Group
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote carries this line in the main quotes list on its Richard Branson page with a citation attached: an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book Reflections on Success (1997). The book is real, Branson is named among its interviewees, and the sentiment matches how Branson tells the story elsewhere in his own voice — but every copy reachable online is lending-restricted or paywalled, so the page itself could not be opened to confirm the wording letter-for-letter.

source.heading: Where the line comes from

docMeta.dd: Interview with Martyn Lewis, BBC news presenter
Citation documented; book text not independently opened

source.excerpt: I became an entrepreneur by mistake. Ever since then I’ve gone into business, not to make money, but because I think I can do it better than it’s been done elsewhere. And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.
trail: Wikiquote’s Richard Branson page ↗ carries the full three-sentence wording in its main quotes list, footnoted “As stated in an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book, Reflections on Success (1997)”. Quote Investigator has no article on this line.

The book is real and the citation is checkable in outline. Wikipedia’s article on Martyn Lewis ↗ lists “Reflections on Success (1997) – interviews with more than 60 notable individuals across a wide range of professions analysing their success”. Lewis was presenting the BBC Six O’Clock News across those years.
Branson is demonstrably one of those interviewees: the publisher’s synopsis on the AbeBooks listing for ISBN 9781852911393 ↗ describes 67 interviews and names Richard Branson among them.

What stops this being fully verified: the Internet Archive’s copy ↗ (Lennard, 1998; catalogued with the note “Previous edition: 1997”) is lending-restricted, so its text cannot be searched. We could not read the page and confirm the sentence letter-for-letter, and we do not claim to have.
source.excerptNote: This is the full three-sentence form as Wikiquote records it — and the aggregators we checked (Lib Quotes, Quotepark, The Cite Site) print all three sentences too. The two-sentence version in the headline above is this site’s own clipping, not evidence about how others quote the line.

source.rightsNote: The work carrying this line, Reflections on Success, was first published in 1997 — far too recent for the public domain in the United States, where copyright protection is the default for anything first published in 1931 or later. The interview format means two interests overlap: the compiler-interviewer and his publisher in the book, and Branson himself in the words he spoke. Treat short quotation with attribution as ordinary fair use and do not reproduce the chapter.

author.name: Richard Branson
author.heading: About Richard Branson
author.metaLine: Born 18 July 1950 · English entrepreneur, founder of the Virgin Group
author.bio: Richard Branson was born in Blackheath, south-east London, on 18 July 1950. He left school young and put out the first issue of a magazine called Student in January 1968 — the venture that, on his own telling, turned him into a businessman against his intentions. He launched the record label Virgin Records in 1972 and built the Virgin name outward from there into airlines, rail, telecoms and spaceflight.

misattribution.heading: How this one gets mangled
misattribution.intro: This is not a stolen-attribution case. Nobody credits it to Steve Jobs or Henry Ford, and no fact-checker has flagged it. What goes wrong is quieter: the citation gets dropped, and Branson’s own opening phrase moves around between retellings.

items.why: The Cite Site ↗ carries all three sentences but attaches no book, no interviewer and no date — leaving readers no way to check it. Quotepark ↗ does keep the Martyn Lewis citation.

He does not always say “by mistake”. Talking to Chase Jarvis he said he became “an entrepreneur by default because I had to worry about the advertising, worry about the distribution, worry about the printing” ↗. Same story, different word — so a “by default” version is not a corruption.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest summary: the citation is real and specific — Wikiquote ↗ ties it to his interview with Martyn Lewis in Reflections on Success (1997), and Lib Quotes and Quotepark carry the same citation — but the book’s text has not been independently checked. Quote it in full, and cite the book.

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: Branson’s claim is not modesty — it is a claim about sequence. He wanted to edit a magazine, not run a company. The first issue of Student appeared in January 1968, and keeping it alive meant selling the advertising and sorting the printing and distribution himself. Business was the tax he paid on the thing he actually wanted to do.

The second sentence is the one that does the work. It sets out a test for entering a market that has nothing to do with margin: not is there money here, but is the incumbent doing this badly enough that I could do it better. That is the logic Branson has used to explain moving the Virgin name from records into airlines, trains and phones — industries with no obvious thread between them except an incumbent he thought was complacent.
context.detailsSummary: The third sentence, and why it changes the meaning
detailsBody: The full quotation runs to three sentences, and the closing one is: “And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.”

Cut it — as any two-sentence quotation of the line does — and it reads as a tidy philosophy of value creation. Keep it and it reads as something closer to irritation: a man starting companies because a service annoyed him. The short form is the one that would fit on a motivational poster; the full one sounds like a person.
context.pull: Not to make money, but because I think I can do it better than it’s been done elsewhere.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Richard Branson page carries the full three-sentence quote in its main quotes list, cited as 'As stated in an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book, Reflections on Success (1997)'.

The Internet Archive catalogue record for Reflections on Success gives: Lewis, Martyn, 1945-; publisher Harpenden: Lennard; date 1998; description note 'Previous edition: 1997'; ISBN 1852911395 / 9781852911393; 960 pages. The item is lending-restricted and its text cannot be searched.

Wikipedia's article on Martyn Lewis lists 'Reflections on Success (1997) – interviews with more than 60 notable individuals across a wide range of professions analysing their success', and records that he presented the BBC Six O'Clock News from 1994 to 1999.
The AbeBooks listing for ISBN 9781852911393 carries a publisher synopsis describing interviews with 67 famous people, and names Richard Branson among the interviewees.

In his CreativeLive interview with Chase Jarvis, Branson says he became 'an entrepreneur by default because I had to worry about the advertising, worry about the distribution, worry about the printing'.

Wikipedia records that Richard Branson was born 18 July 1950 in Blackheath, London; that the first issue of Student appeared in January 1968; and that he launched the record label Virgin Records in 1972.

Lib Quotes prints the full three-sentence quote, closing with 'And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it's been done by other people.', and cites 'An interview with Martyn Lewis in his book, Reflections on Success (1997)'. Re-checked 8 Sep 2026: it does not truncate the line.
The Cite Site reproduces all three sentences of the quote but provides no book, publication or date as a source.
Quotepark reproduces all three sentences with the citation 'As stated in an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book, Reflections on Success (1997)'.
